summary: Round-2 feature testing of StudyAce (auto-name on upload, preview original, Walkthrough, Study Guide + checklist, Key Terms, quiz formula-mix, clean formatting). Backend: 12/12 new pytest tests PASS on top of the existing 20/20 regression suite. Frontend E2E via Playwright verified: login -> course -> Documents (preview PDF-frame OR open-original-btn for .txt), Walkthrough player (step, prev/next, reveal-answer, progress bar, source ref, Physics of Projectile Motion 19 steps rendered cleanly), Study Guide viewer opens with 'Quiz Revision Checklist' + 10 fillable checkboxes, Key Terms viewer lists 7 terms alphabetically (Acceleration→Work), AI Chat replies come back. Auto-name verified via backend (feat1786326500 seed doc predates the feature so name==original filename). ONE CRITICAL FORMATTING BUG found: the AI (Gemini 3 Flash) occasionally emits MALFORMED [[frac:...]] tokens (extra `]]`, or content spillover like `[[frac:1|2]]mv²]]`), which the RichText regex parser cannot recover from, so users see literal `[[frac:1|2` and `]]` and `mv²]]` inside the rendered study guide AND chat replies. This directly violates the CLEAN FORMATTING requirement ('no raw [[frac ... ]] tokens visible; stacked fractions render via <span data-testid=frac>').

ui_bugs.issue: Literal '[[frac:1|2]]mv²]]', '[[frac:∆s|∆t]]]]' etc. show up as visible text inside guide-content because Gemini output has malformed frac tokens (extra `]]`, content OUTSIDE `]]`). Parser only strips well-formed `[[frac:num|den]]` so the stray `]]` and trailing `mv²]]` leak. See screenshot /app/test_reports/frontend_final.png and /app/test_reports/chat_final.png.
Same as above — literal '[[frac:1|2' and 'gt²]]' rendered as plain text in the reply body (e.g. y = v₀ × sin(θ) × t − [[frac:1|2 gt²]]).

issues: Missing DialogDescription / aria-describedby warning still logged (non-blocking, carried over from iter 1).

action_items: Fix the malformed-fraction rendering bug. Two complementary fixes are recommended: (a) Tighten the LLM prompt / FORMAT_RULES to REJECT patterns like '[[frac:X|Y]]Z]]' and '[[frac:X|Y]]]]' — instruct the model to always write ONE well-formed [[frac:NUM|DEN]] per stacked fraction with no trailing brackets or extra ]]; (b) Make RichText.js parser resilient — after the frac regex, also STRIP any orphan '[[frac:...' openers or bare ']]' remaining in the text (e.g. run `.replace(/\]\]/g,'').replace(/\[\[frac:[^\]]*$/,'')` on the residual chunks before passing to ReactMarkdown), and/or post-process the LLM output server-side to normalise these tokens before storage. Repro: log in as feat1786326500@test.com / pass1234 -> Physics course -> Study Guide tab -> Read Guide -> observe literal '[[frac:1|2]]mv²]]' in Kinetic Energy section. Also visible in AI Chat when asking about projectile motion.
(Minor, carried over) Add DialogDescription to Radix DialogContent components to silence a11y console warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: RichText.renderTokens (/app/frontend/src/components/RichText.js) is not defensive: any LLM deviation from the strict `[[frac:num|den]]` shape (extra brackets, content outside the closer, missing pipe) causes raw tokens to leak into the final DOM. Consider a two-pass sanitiser (strip bare ']]' after a completed frac, drop stray '[[frac:' openers with no matching closer) or use a real tokeniser.
server.py FORMAT_RULES should include an explicit anti-example for the malformed pattern (e.g. WRONG: [[frac:1|2]]mv²]] — RIGHT: [[frac:1|2 mv²|1]] or (1/2)mv² or [[frac:mv²|2]]).

generate_walkthrough/generate_study_guide/generate_key_terms all silently trust LLM output structure (no validation/post-processing). At minimum they could run a regex sanitiser before persisting to Mongo so bad tokens never reach the client.

Study-guide checklist re-renders after PATCH — checkbox handles get detached; UI is fine (Playwright locator re-resolves) but any code doing DOM refs would break. Consider a stable key strategy in RichText input renderer.
download_document is correct now (cookie auth) — good fix. preview iframe uses blob URL — no auth-in-URL leak, nice.

success_rate.frontend: 85% — all navigational + interactive flows work; formatting bug in 2 surfaces (Study Guide + Chat) when material has stacked fractions

context_for_next_testing_agent: Repro the formatting bug quickly: `curl` login as feat1786326500 -> GET /api/study-guides/<gid> -> grep for '[[frac:' matches with `]]]]` or `]]mv` in content. After main agent fixes prompt/parser, re-run /app/backend/tests/test_studyace_features.py::TestStudyGuide and re-check the guide viewer + chat for stray '[[' or ']]' characters. Key-terms first-line text extraction returns duplicated names ('AccelerationAcceleration') — that's a Playwright text_content quirk (h3 + source cite both contain the term); not a real UI defect — visually the term appears once in the card.
rca of the issue: Gemini 3 Flash occasionally emits malformed frac tokens in study-guide markdown and chat replies (observed shapes: `[[frac:∆s|∆t]]]]` with 4 closing brackets, and `[[frac:1|2]]mv²]]` where the intended stacked fraction is (1/2)mv² but the model split it as frac(1,2) followed by literal mv² and a stray `]]`). The frontend regex `/\[\[frac:([^|\]]*)\|([^\]]*)\]\]/` correctly matches the FIRST well-formed `[[frac:1|2]]` but leaves the trailing `mv²]]` untouched, which then goes to ReactMarkdown and renders as visible text. Fix: strengthen prompt (explicit anti-example) + add defensive server-side / client-side sanitiser that strips orphan `]]` and unmatched `[[frac:` sequences.
